\chapter{Vuestro --- The Last Possessive}
\label{ch:vuestro}
\hlchaptermodality{254}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can use every possessive in the set.}

I can use every possessive in the set.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[vuestro]{vuestro — the last possessive}

\label{lesson:ES-C65-vuestro}



\begin{quote}
\emph{Nuestra casa} — our house. And \emph{vosotros} — you all.

One possessive is still missing, and the pair you just said gives it away.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the pair}]
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{} & \textbf{} \\
\midrule
\emph{nosotros} $\to$ & \emph{\textbf{nuestro}} \emph{libro}, \emph{\textbf{nuestra}} \emph{casa} \\
\emph{vosotros} $\to$ & \emph{\textbf{vuestro}} \emph{libro}, \emph{\textbf{vuestra}} \emph{casa} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

Same ending, same agreement, same position in front of the noun. Once you have seen it beside \emph{nuestro} there is nothing left to learn — which is why it has been safe to leave until last.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{culture}
And that completes the set. Say them in order:

\emph{mi · tu · su · nuestro · vuestro · su}

Six, and only two of them — \emph{nuestro} and \emph{vuestro} — change for gender. \emph{Mi}, \emph{tu} and \emph{su} do not care whether the thing is masculine or feminine; they only change for \textbf{number}.

As with every \emph{vosotros} form, you will meet \emph{vuestro} mainly in Spain, and you will read it everywhere. It costs one word to know it and it closes the set.
\end{culture}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{nuestra casa}, then \emph{vuestra casa}
  \item all six, in order
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which possessive goes with \emph{vosotros}? (\emph{\textbf{Vuestro}}.)

And how many of the six change for gender? (\textbf{Two.})
\end{tcolorbox}
